questiontext.text:
We have simulated data sets giving the crop yield for different crops. The outcome variable is the Crop Yield, and the explanatory variables are:

  • Soil Quality Index Score – a numerical variable ranging from 1–10, where higher scores represent better soil quality.
  • Crop Planted – a factor variable indicating the type of crop planted (Corn, Rice, Sorghum).
  • Region – a factor variable specifying the region in which the crop is grown.
  • Pest Density – a numerical variable indicating how many pests are present.
  • Pest Susceptibility – a factor variable with three levels (low, medium, high) indicating how susceptible the crop is to pests.
  • Fertiliser Level – a numerical variable giving the concentration of fertiliser used.

The following visualisation shows the Crop Yield on the \(Y\) axis and the three different Crop Types on the \(X\) axis. For each crop type, we see a boxplot that summarises the distribution of yield values.

One additional data dimension is shown using the colour aesthetic:

Visual Element What It Represents
X-axis Crop Type (Corn, Rice, Sorghum)
Y-axis Crop Yield
Colour Pest Density (darker = fewer pests, lighter = more pests)

Each point represents an individual observation — the yield of a particular crop grown in a specific field, with a given pest density.

---

The Goal

We are examining whether crop yield is influenced by the type of crop planted and whether there's any relationship between yield and pest density.

---

Interpreting the Plot

  • Crop Type: We see that the yield tends to be lowest for Corn, higher for Rice, and highest for Sorghum. This suggests that crop type is correlated with crop yield.
  • Pest Density (Colour): Although colour shows pest density, the yield values do not show a strong trend across the colour gradient. That means there's no clear correlation between pest density and yield in this plot.
---

---

Your Task

Download this data set. This is not the same as the data used to make the graphic above.

Create a similar visualisation - try plotting crop type on the X-axis, yield on the Y-axis, and using colour to show pest density.

---

falsefeedback.text:
Not quite. Have a look at the boxplots. The boxplots display a steady increase between the different crops. This implies that there is a difference between crop type and yield.

More specifically, we can see that Sorghum tends to result in the highest yield when we compare the boxplot to the y axis.

For more information on interpreting boxplots, see here.
